summary: Rate-shedding during rollout migration leaves stale pin shards causing mixed-model responses for enterprise tenant
description: Customer reports intermittent mixed-model outputs and a spike in latency/errors during a staged canary migration in us-east-1. Symptoms started after we increased canary weight for their tenant as part of a scheduled promote. Impact: 8% of requests for tenant 'acme-health' were routed to a legacy variant for ~12 minutes, producing unexpected tokenization/formatting differences and a small increase in 5xx streaming disconnects. Root cause suspected to involve stale pin shard state not being fully flushed when orchestrator rate-shedding triggered partial migration retries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In prod us-east-1, start a weighted canary promote for tenant acme-health from variant A -> variant B (10% -> 50% over 10m).
2) Apply autoscaler synthetic load to push nodes into rate-shed policy (simulate noisy neighbor by creating burst of short-lived streams).
3) Observe orchestrator logs for commit windows and pin-shard flush events; check edge-proxy routing decisions and cookie/affinity headers.
4) Reproduce client requests that rely on streaming and model-specific tokenization to detect mixed outputs.

investigation_notes: 14:10 - Initial triage (Maya): customer reports quality regression and intermittent 5xxs starting exactly when canary weight was bumped.

14:20 - SRE (Liam) observed a cluster-wide rate-shed event from the autoscaler coincident with the canary promote window. Orchestrator shows commit-window retries where shard flush acknowledgement from edge was not seen before a migration retry.

14:35 - Hypothesis: when the orchestrator retried the commit due to rate-shed, it wrote a new pin-shard but the edge-proxy still served requests from an older pin-shard (TTL mismatch + cache not invalidated), creating a cohort split. Some streams followed new variant, some old -> mixed outputs.
14:50 - Confirmed via distributed trace that request X and request Y from same session were routed to different variants; trace ids: trace-a1b2 (variant-A), trace-c3d4 (variant-B).

15:05 - We reproduced locally by forcing rate-shed and observing commit-window retry path; edge cache invalidation was not issued on retry path due to a short-circuit return in coordinator code (PR suspected).
comments: 2026-03-12T15:12Z - Maya (Support): Contacted Acme HealthTech (Sarah Kim) to confirm impact window and collect example request IDs and affected timestamps.
2026-03-12T15:25Z - Sarah Kim (Acme HealthTech): We saw unusual tokenization in chat responses and a handful of streaming resets. Attached sample request_id: rq-20260312-77a.
2026-03-12T16:02Z - Liam (SRE): Added debug logging to orchestrator commit path and initiated edge cache invalidation for tenant acme-health as an immediate mitigation.
2026-03-12T16:20Z - Dev (serving-runtime): Noted a codepath (Coordinator.commit_retry) that returns early on rate-shed and skips cache-broadcast; raising PR to add guaranteed invalidation on retries.
2026-03-12T17:00Z - Maya (Support): Customer confirms mixed outputs decreased after edge invalidation; they still request a postmortem and a permanent fix timeline.
resolution: Workaround applied: immediate edge-cache invalidation for tenant acme-health and manual flush of pin-shard entries across orchestrator replicas. Customer traffic returned to expected variant consistency. Long-term fix: code change to Coordinator.commit_retry to ensure cache-broadcast/invalidation is executed on retry paths even when rate-shed is active (PR 4821). Follow-up: add unit + e2e test to simulate rate-shed/migration and add monitoring alert for commit-window mismatches.
